readme: # Hex Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and it pastes. ## How it works - hold the shortcut, speak, then let go - Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in - the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine - experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar ## What it does - hold the shortcut to dictate, or set Shortcut mode to Tap to start and stop with a press - the text lands at the cursor in whatever app you're in - Option-Shift-V pastes the last dictation again (Ctrl-Alt-V on Windows and Linux) - History keeps your dictations, searchable, for 7 days by default - Output runs every dictation through steps you choose (word replacements, built-in cleanups, your own scripts, an optional OpenCode rewrite), with different steps per app or website - Vocabulary is one list of names Hex should know; Whisper and Qwen3-ASR read it while transcribing, Parakeet models read it with Labs › Vocabulary help on, and the OpenCode rewrite uses it - Annotate records the screen while you draw and talk, on macOS, Linux and Windows (GNOME Wayland needs Labs › Annotate on GNOME) - an authenticated local API and the [TypeScript SDK](sdk/typescript/README.md) transcribe with the same model, for your own tools - Meetings is a macOS lab that records a call and writes the transcript Output and History: ## Speech models Hex downloads one model the first time it runs and transcribes with it on your machine from then on. On an English system that's Parakeet Unified English: it writes while you talk, so the text is ready when you let go. Other languages start with the model recommended for them. That model also serves meetings and `hex transcribe`. Settings' picker offers more, among others: - Parakeet v3: 25 European languages, and it hears which one you speak - Cohere Transcribe: the fewest wrong words, in 14 languages; a big download - Whisper large-v3-turbo: almost any language, and it reads your vocabulary - Qwen3-ASR 0.6B: Chinese and 29 more, and it reads your vocabulary - SenseVoice Small: Chinese, Japanese, Korean and English; a small download - Nemotron 3.5 ASR: writes while you talk, in 27 languages - Granite Speech 5.0: IBM's model, seven languages, with punctuation - one-language models: ivrit.ai Whisper for Hebrew, GigaAM v3 for Russian, NB-Whisper for Norwegian, KB-Whisper for Swedish, QwenCleo-ASR for Egyptian Arabic - more English models: Parakeet v2 and Underdog Bark 3.0 Add a GGUF model of your own with "Add model file…" in the picker; see [your own speech models](docs/features/own-models.md). ## Downloads Stable is the current release. Dev is the newest build of `dev` and updates itself from the dev channel. The [changelog](https://anoma.ly/hex/changelog) says what each release changed. | Platform | Stable | Dev | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS (Apple silicon) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/macos-arm64-dmg) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/macos-arm64-dmg) | | Windows x64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-x64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-x64-setup) | | Windows ARM64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-arm64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-arm64-setup) | | Linux x86_64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64) | | Linux x86_64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-deb) | | Linux x86_64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-rpm) | | Linux ARM64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64) | | Linux ARM64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-deb) | | Linux ARM64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-rpm) | Or install with: - Homebrew: `brew install --cask anomalyco/tap/hex` - AUR: `yay -S hex-bin` - install script (Linux): `curl -fsSL https://anoma.ly/hex/install-linux.sh | sh` - Nix (Linux): `nix profile add github:anomalyco/hex` ## Command line `hex transcribe meeting.m4a` prints a recording's transcript, whether or not the app is running. It reads WAV, AIFF, CAF, FLAC, MP3, Ogg, WebM, and MP4/M4A/MOV, including a video's soundtrack. The same `hex` controls the running app (`hex status`, `hex dictation`, `hex settings`); see [`docs/cli.md`](docs/cli.md). On macOS the CLI is inside the app. Homebrew links it for you; otherwise link it somewhere on your `PATH` that you own: ```sh ln -s /Applications/Hex.app/Contents/MacOS/hex ~/.local/bin/hex ``` Linux and Windows installs put `hex` on your `PATH`. More docs are in [`docs/`](docs/README.md). ## Contributing We don't take pull requests. [Open an issue](https://github.com/anomalyco/hex/issues) describing the bug or idea, and our agents usually turn it around fast. MIT licensed.
